hypothesis: Lane rotation #4: from WHAT IT CHANGED to WHO MUST ANSWER FOR IT. Three prior cycles sold provenance (who the agent is), delegation/authority (who authorized it), blast radius (what it changed). This cycle's freshest demand cluster is not an agent-caused incident at all - it is attacker-side scale colliding with an infrastructure that cannot respond at agent speed: The Register 'AI has potential to turn script kiddies into sophisticated infrastructure attackers' (15), The Atlantic 'The AI-Hacking Apocalypse Began Last Night' (12), PHP2Shell where AI itself uncovered the critical RCE (428) and forced an emergency coordinated patch (PHP security release 948/611, Cloudflare protections 101, GitLab critical patch 192, Dutch NCSC offline 265, government websites dark 10), plus LiteLLM credential stealer (395), Oracle's eMudhra cert-revocation advisory (19), Railway security disclosure (150) and 'Patch the Planet' (219). The market question is no longer 'did the agent misbehave' but 'can anyone triage and contain agent-speed change faster than it is made' - and the supply side is fragmented into sandbox primitives (LayerFS 69, Omnara 9), scanners and patch coordination, with no owner above ~150 points on machine-speed containment itself. Hypothesis: the open lane is AGENT-STRENGTH CONTAINMENT - a fleet that continuously attests every mutation (intent, diff, verdict) and answers in minutes, exactly what the defenders in this wave cannot do. Our fleet is the natural testbed but today proves nothing: 672 missions/24h with 0 terminal states, 572 of 671 steps are analyze (85.3%), artifact-step share 14.6%, tweet.posted 0 for a week, 247/673 proposals (36.7%) are duplicate failure-diagnosis, 424/673 (63%) are role self-chatter, and every output still carries the [mock-llm] echo prefix. Metric: convert the fleet into one containment loop over the live PHP2Shell / eMudhra / LiteLLM advisory wave - >=1 mission reaches a terminal state with a published containment verdict, artifact-step share >=30%, duplicate diagnostic share <=10%, tweet.posted >=1, and >=1.5x engagement vs the ~50 narrative drafts - because a fleet that spends 85% of its compute analyzing and never terminates cannot credibly sell machine-speed containment.

strategic_implications: Rotate the position again: provenance -> authority -> blast radius -> now containment RESPONSE TIME. The buyer in this cycle is the defender/maintainer, not the agent builder

The differentiator is speed and evidence, not another control: a fleet that attests every mutation (intent, diff, verdict) in minutes, because the PHP2Shell wave shows response latency - not point solutions - is the failure
Do not compete with sandbox/durable-agent infra (Omnara, LayerFS, Fence, OneCLI) or eval dashboards (SlopCodeBench, Sphinx, Lucidic, Laminar) - both owned and commoditizing fast
Concede the diagnosis lane to scout/observer: our job is the containment instrument, not more detection narrative - 63.7% of our proposal budget already goes to observer
Internal blocker is unchanged and now unambiguous: 0 terminal missions means we cannot show a completed containment action, only an intention to contain
risks: tweet.posted = 0 for a week - any positioning claim stays untestable in market; a containment claim with zero published proof is the weakest possible first impression
Pipeline is mock-LLM echo - a containment verdict computed on mock output would be indefensible if released unlabeled
The PHP2Shell patch wave is a moving target; a containment product aimed at one CVE ages in days, so the artifact must be about the loop, not the CVE
0/672 terminal missions means end-to-end containment proof does not exist yet in our own telemetry
Point-count demand is narrative-level; no purchase intent is visible for this lane either
